news.title: An eval harness found what qualitative review couldn't: AI models are most confident when wrong
news.summary_raw: There is a step in the development process for large language model (LLM)-assisted tooling that most teams skip because it's tedious, time-consuming, and doesn't produce results visible to end users: Verifying that what the model is saying is actually correct. Not fluent, not coherent, not topically relevant — correct in the sense of accurately identifying the right answer to the specific problem the tool was built to solve.The gap between "this output sounds right to me" and
news.summary: An evaluation harness found that AI models are most confident when their answers are wrong, highlighting a gap between model confidence and correctness. This issue arises from a common oversight in the development process for large language model-assisted tooling.
